criteria.text: wc2 <file> --top N outputs exactly N words with the most frequent first; equal frequencies break alphabetically

grader.evidence: bin/wc2.js parses `--top N` and slices the sorted entries; src/count.js:7 sorts by `b[1]-a[1] || a[0].localeCompare(b[0])`. Verified directly: `node bin/wc2.js task.md --top 5` prints exactly 5 lines (json 4 / the 4 / wc 4 / a 3 / file 3) — descending count, alphabetical within each tie group. sortWords(countWords('b a c a b c d')) returns [[a,2],[b,2],[c,2],[d,1]]. `--top 999` on a 60-unique-word file prints 60 lines (graceful when N exceeds available), `--top 0` prints nothing with exit 0. Non-integer/negative/missing N (`--top`, `--top abc`, `--top -1`, `--top 2.5`) all exit 2 with usage. t

grader.evidence: bin/wc2.js prints `JSON.stringify(entries.map(([word, count]) => ({ word, count })))` from the same sorted `entries` used by the line path.
